blocks.heading: Routes Scale Furthest, Strongest First
blocks.sourceSectionTitle: Which routes scale furthest, strongest first

rows: Engineer who ships tools or takes contract work
Code can be sold again and again as a project, a tool or a small product, so income is not capped by one employer. It still needs proof and a first client.
Pipeline and data-model skills sell as projects to firms with messy data, and data engineering rose from 4.3% to 7.7% of tech postings between July and October 2026.
Knowing one industry lets you sell analysis to small firms in it, but you must plan the layer yourself: a clear offer, proof and first clients.
Engineer on a fixed IT services package
Raises follow the company band and fresher packages sit near Rs 3 to 4 lakh. Treat it as a first step and keep a skill running that can grow on its own.
Standard reports and charts are the easiest layer for templates and AI tools to repeat, and pay climbs in small steady steps.

items.text: Check what your family can carry while you learn.

blocks.heading: Budget Check: Data Analyst Vs Software

figures.source: An illustration, not a real fee: if a family sets aside Rs 4 lakh for all of a student's learning, about Rs 40,000 is our suggested limit for one course, and Rs 80,000 is where extra evidence is needed. visuals.heading: What Lifts an Engineer's Pay

items.text: Move from an IT services firm to a GCC or product company once you have one deployed project and clear interview answers.
Go deep in one area employers pay for, such as backend systems, cloud or data pipelines, instead of touching five tools.
Own one feature or service from start to finish, with tests and a note on what broke and how you fixed it.
Learn to explain a trade-off in plain words to a manager who does not code.

blocks.heading: AI and Pay for Both Roles

items.text: Use AI to draft SQL or code, then test every answer against real data.
Write down each time the AI was wrong and how you caught it.
Pick one real problem at work or in a project and finish it end to end.
